title: 3-SAT: brute force vs Schöning vs PPSZ
problem_statement: Given a Boolean formula in conjunctive normal form with at most 3 literals per clause, decide whether some assignment satisfies it.

algorithms.name: brute force
algorithms.pseudocode: for each assignment a: if a satisfies F: yes

algorithms.name: Schöning's random walk
algorithms.idea: Random initial assignment; repeatedly flip a random variable of an unsatisfied clause; restart after 3n steps.

algorithms.name: PPSZ / biased-PPSZ
algorithms.idea: Random variable order; set each variable by bounded-width resolution if forced, else randomly.
algorithms.time_complexity: O(1.308^n) (PPSZ; Hertli 2014 in general); O(1.307^n) (biased-PPSZ, Hansen et al. 2019)
algorithms.correctness: Paturi et al. 2005; Hertli 2014; Hansen, Kaplan, Zamir, Zwick 2019.

relationship: 2^n -> (4/3)^n -> 1.307^n: exponential to better exponential. 3-SAT is NP-complete (Cook 1971), so a polynomial algorithm would prove P = NP. The Exponential Time Hypothesis conjectures that some base > 1 is unavoidable.

caveats: 2-SAT is solvable in linear time; see notes/boundary-2sat-vs-3sat.md. That is a boundary between problems, not a same-problem pair.
notes: Path to V1: brute force vs Schöning (randomized, so V1 needs the satisfiable/unsatisfiable answers to agree with high probability over planted and random instances).
